item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is in my opinion a classic case of an SCP that would have been a lot better had the author stopped earlier.

When I started reading I thought "okay, a tiger that makes people think it's a cat. Pretty interesting and potentially creepy because it might go into a town unnoticed", but as I read further it actually became less and less interesting to me as the author was saying too much about it, which lessened its aura of mystery.

+ spoilered for size
- spoilered for size

For example, why give it a psychic power that forces people to go pet it? Why can't it just be people going to pet it because they think it's cute? Why does it even need to conceal its appearance if it can just do this?

Another thing I really wasn't a fan of was how the more it went, the more it insisted about how this tiger prefers human preys as it felt like another case of attempting to make a normally only unnerving SCP scary by randomly having it target humans specifically, not to mention the explanation given for it is really not satisfactory.

It "adapted to take advantage of the largest available food source" (which, by the way, is a rather questionable conclusion to reach from that data)? How does that make sense? The average tiger wouldn't even consider humans as a food source, and that's a pretty bad adaptation considering humans are also the prey most likely to kill it (there's a reason most wild animals have learned to avoid humans).

And if the adaptation is because of the largest available food source, why didn't it adapt to eat ants or something like that, considering they far outnumber us, are incapable of killing it and will be more common in SCP-247's natural habitat (not many humans in the jungle or the savannah)?

I also have a few problems with the tone. One of the required traits for becoming a retrieval team agent is "low empathy scores". Why, oh why do people insist on making the SCP Foundation this cartoonishly evil entity that it clearly isn't?

Look, if the agents, need to do something morally questionable for the sake of containing an SCP subject, I think they'll do it regardless of their "empathy score", you don't have to make "be evil" a requirement and no matter how much you sugar coat it with technical jargon, that's literally what you did.

Similarly, the SCP Foundation codenaming Mobile Task Force Iota-5 "Tiger Bait" is just… urgh.

All in all, I'm keeping my vote neutral. I like the idea of a tiger that disguises itself as a harmless animal but not so much the… everything else.
Like I said, I think removing the references to hunting Humans specifically and the seemingly redundant psychic powers would actually make it a lot more interesting by keeping it uncanny.

I also feel the test logs don't really add anything. Maybe keep a couple of them for flavour but most of them really don't need to be there.

item.title: Old memes
item.content:encoded:
There're some details here that were considered appropriate back in early 2010, when this was first submitted, but now strike me as completely off.

"In the unlikely event that there are any survivors of a containment violation, they will be demoted to D-class."

Not only is the whole "demoted to D-class" notion silly, it presumes that everyone involved in a containment violation will be equally at fault. I suggest that this be removed entirely.

ALSO

"Individuals in this field also show extreme reluctance to harm or allow others to harm SCP-247, even while [DATA EXPUNGED]."

This is obviously "even while being mauled to death by SCP-247"; it's the only thing that makes sense here, given that this is 247's motivation, and there's no reason to expunge it. Phrase it more prettily, sure, but not expunge it.
